newsitem.title: EGYPT: El Arish selected for Egypt's natgas exports.
newsitem.headline: El Arish selected for Egypt's natgas exports.

text.p: Egypt has selected the north Sinai town of El Arish as the site of a terminal for natural gas exports to Turkey and other countries in the eastern Mediterranean, a government newspaper said on Saturday.

Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi has told the state's Egyptian General Petroleum Corp to reserve 400 acres (160 hectares) of land near El Arish airport for the project, which will cost four billion pounds ($1.2 billion), the newspaper Akhbar el-Yom said.
"The terminal will export gas to Turkey, Israel, Lebanon, Jordan and Palestine. Building work will begin within the next few months," it added.
The report made no distinction between exports of liquefied natural gas by tanker and exports by pipeline -- the obvious choice for countries which have a land border with Egypt.

Officials at EGPC and at Amoco, the main foreign company in Egyptian gas exports, were not available to comment on Saturday but the Italian energy group ENI had proposed El Arish as a natural hub for Egyptian gas exports.
In November Amoco signed a memorandum of understanding with Egypt and Turkey on exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the Nile Delta to Turkey.
Jordanian Energy Minister Hashem Dabbas said on Wednesday that Amoco had also signed a deal to study building a pipeline to export Egyptian gas to Jordan.

The minister said the pipeline would cross the Sinai peninsula, pass under the Red Sea and pump gas to Jordan's southern port of Aqaba, hooking up to a national gas grid which Amoco is also planning as part of the project.
Egypt and Israel have been in talks on Egyptian gas exports for several years but these have made less progress than those with Turkey and Jordan.
Most of the Egyptian gas allocated for export is under the Mediterranean off the Nile Delta, about 150 to 200 km (90 to 125 miles) west of El Arish.

Under one scenario proposed by ENI, Amoco's partner in some of the Nile Delta gasfields, El Arish could also serve as export hub for natural gas piped from the Gulf state of Qatar, which has the third largest gas reserves in the world.
